Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Makhno expressed optimism to them about the possibility of revolution in Spain, due to the organisational abilities of the Spanish anarchists, and expressed hope that he would live to participate in it.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: In July _____, the French police smuggled Durruti and Ascaso into Belgium, where they were received by the Belgian anarchist Marcel Dieu
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In July 1927, the French police smuggled Durruti and Ascaso into Belgium, where they were received by the Belgian anarchist Marcel Dieu.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Facing deportation back to Spain, they were given refuge by the pacifist Émile Bouchet at his home in Joigny.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In early November 1927, Ascaso and Durruti arrived in Lyon.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: They also became involved in debates over the relationship between the CNT and the Spanish anarchist movement.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: Their ideas were rejected by more orthodox anarchists, who accused them of "anarcho-_____"
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Their ideas were rejected by more orthodox anarchists, who accused them of "anarcho-Bolshevism".

Buenaventura Durruti.question: Durruti and _____ also aligned themselves against proposals to establish sections of the CNT in France, as they believed it would divert attention away from revolutionary initiatives in Spain
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti and Ascaso upheld the revolutionary potential of both the proletariat and the peasantry in Spain, and believed that anarchists ought to accelerate the revolutionary process by encouraging revolutionary initiatives and staying focused on long-term goals over short-term material improvements. Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In January 1928, Durruti and Ascaso went to Paris, where they heard news from Ricardo Sanz and Joaquín Cortés about the Spanish and Argentine anarchist movements. Buenaventura Durruti.question: They were imprisoned from April to October _____ and, after their release, were still unable to secure visas so they could leave France
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In January 1928, Durruti and Ascaso went to Paris, where they heard news from Ricardo Sanz and Joaquín Cortés about the Spanish and Argentine anarchist movements. They were imprisoned from April to October 1928 and, after their release, were still unable to secure visas so they could leave France.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In January 1928, Durruti and Ascaso went to Paris, where they heard news from Ricardo Sanz and Joaquín Cortés about the Spanish and Argentine anarchist movements. Buenaventura Durruti.question: They initially attempted to secure a visa from the _____, but when its embassy required them to pledge their loyalty to the socialist state, they refused

Buenaventura Durruti.question: There they attended a conference of the _____' Association (IWA), where they clashed with Federica Montseny over questions of revolutionary leadership
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: There they attended a conference of the International Workers' Association (IWA), where they clashed with Federica Montseny over questions of revolutionary leadership.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Despite interventions by members of the _____, they were unable to secure asylum, and were expelled following objections by the Catholic Centre Party
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Despite interventions by members of the Social Democratic Party, they were unable to secure asylum, and were expelled following objections by the Catholic Centre Party.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Durruti and _____ subsequently decided to return to Mexico
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti and Ascaso subsequently decided to return to Mexico. However, when Durruti and Ascaso arrived in Belgium in early 1929, they discovered the country had relaxed its immigration laws and become a safe haven for Spanish exiles.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: However, when Durruti and Ascaso arrived in Belgium in early _____, they discovered the country had relaxed its immigration laws and become a safe haven for Spanish exiles
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: However, when Durruti and Ascaso arrived in Belgium in early 1929, they discovered the country had relaxed its immigration laws and become a safe haven for Spanish exiles.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: They decided to send most of the money back to Rocker and remain in Brussels, where Durruti found work as a metalworker.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: Ida Mett recalled that his skills as a mechanic meant that he could easily find work, even during the _____

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti also set up a newspaper, La Voz de Libertaria, together with Dieu, and propagandised for the FAI.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: During their time in _____, Durruti and Ascaso were involved in numerous conspiracies
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: During their time in Brussels, Durruti and Ascaso were involved in numerous conspiracies.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The Catalan nationalist leader Francesc Macià also attempted to solicit their support for a rebellion, but they refused.

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The following month, on 28 January 1930, Miguel Primo de Rivera was removed from power and his dictatorship in Spain collapsed.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: As the _____ anarcho-syndicalist movement was revived, many anarchist exiles began to return to the country
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: As the Spanish anarcho-syndicalist movement was revived, many anarchist exiles began to return to the country.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti and Ascaso were themselves tempted to return, but as many of the repressive structures of the dictatorship remained in place, Liberto Callejas cautioned them to wait for the right moment. The following day, Durruti and Ascaso reunited with Ricardo Sanz, who told them about the CNT's role in installing the republican government of Lluís Companys; Durruti and Ascaso regarded this to have been a mistake.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: For this position, they were denounced as "anarcho-Bolsheviks" by other members of the CNT and as "infantile revolutionaries" by Marxists.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: Upon his arrival in _____, Durruti initially stayed at Luis Riera's house in Sant Martí de Provençals

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: As many former members of Los Solidarios remained in prison, Durruti and Ascaso had set about agitating for their immediate release.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: At a meeting of the CNT at _____ïc, on 18–19 April, Durruti gave a speech about the new Republic

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Among his own demands were the release of political prisoners, the abolition of the Civil Guard and the separation of church and state.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: In preparation for _____' Day, Durruti was delegated to accompany foreign anarchists that would be visiting Barcelona, including the French anarchist Louis Lecoin
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: In preparation for International Workers' Day, Durruti was delegated to accompany foreign anarchists that would be visiting Barcelona, including the French anarchist Louis Lecoin.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: When writing to his family on 6 May _____, Durruti advised them not to come to Barcelona, as his life at the time was too busy
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: When writing to his family on 6 May 1931, Durruti advised them not to come to Barcelona, as his life at the time was too busy. By June 1931, Durruti was constantly occupied with meetings, speaking at rallies and attending to other responsibilities.

On 11 May, he sent them another letter, informing them that Morin had arrived from Paris, that he had managed to find a job and that he was looking for a house.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: At the welcome rally at the _____ of Communications, Rocker was overwhelmed by the more than 15,000 attendees

Buenaventura Durruti.question: Durruti's mother then pressed his sister Rosa to travel to _____ and visit him
Buenaventura Durruti.fact: Durruti's mother then pressed his sister Rosa to travel to Barcelona and visit him.

Buenaventura Durruti.question: She reported that Durruti and _____ lived in squalid conditions with few possessions; Morin, who was pregnant at the time, slept on an empty bed base without a mattress

Buenaventura Durruti.question: It was only when _____ de Guzmán, editor of the independent anarchist newspaper La Tierra, approached Durruti for comment that his thoughts on the matter were publicised

Buenaventura Durruti.question: Durruti was later expelled from the _____' Union, after he accused the signatory Ricard Fornells of collaborating with political parties, without evidence

Buenaventura Durruti.fact: The Spanish press branded Durruti, Ascaso and Joan Garcia Oliver as "public enemies", culminating with Ascaso's arrest in October 1931.

Buenaventura Durruti.subject: Indian Languages
Buenaventura Durruti.question: When he finally spoke at the rally, Durruti declared that his arrest for attempting to assassinate _____ XIII proved that Spain was still effectively ruled as a monarchy
